tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are the speakers mainly talking about?

options.A: A driving test.
options.B: A video game.
options.C: Traffic routes.
options.D: Cargo logistics.

questions.cn: 两位说话人主要在谈什么？

optionsCn.A: 一场驾照考试。
optionsCn.B: 一个电子游戏。
optionsCn.C: 交通路线。
optionsCn.D: 货物物流。

questions.stem: What does the man say about the driving simulator?

options.A: He found it instructive and realistic.
options.B: He bought it when touring Europe.
options.C: He was really drawn to its other versions.
options.D: He introduced it to his brother last year.

questions.cn: 关于这个驾驶模拟器，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他觉得它既有教益又逼真。
optionsCn.B: 他是在欧洲旅行时买的。
optionsCn.C: 他真的很喜欢它的其他版本。
optionsCn.D: 他去年把它介绍给了他哥哥。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she really appreciates?

options.A: Traveling all over the country.
options.B: Driving from one city to another.
options.C: The details in the driving simulator.
options.D: The key role of the logistics industry.

questions.cn: 女士说她真的很欣赏什么？

optionsCn.A: 走遍全国各地。
optionsCn.B: 从一个城市开到另一个城市。
optionsCn.C: 驾驶模拟器里的细节。
optionsCn.D: 物流行业的关键作用。

questions.stem: What outcome does the woman expect from the driving simulator?

options.A: Clearer road signs.
options.B: More people driving safely.
options.C: Stricter traffic rules.
options.D: More self-driving trucks on the road.

questions.cn: 女士期待这个驾驶模拟器带来什么结果？

optionsCn.A: 更清晰的路标。
optionsCn.B: 更多人安全驾驶。
optionsCn.C: 更严格的交通规则。
optionsCn.D: 路上有更多自动驾驶卡车。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: F: This is unbelievable, unlike any video game I've ever played before.
lines.cn: F：这真是难以置信，和我以前玩过的任何电子游戏都不一样。

lines.t: F: It's so boring, yet so relaxing at the same time.
lines.cn: F：它这么无聊，同时却这么放松。

lines.t: F: How did you hear about this driving simulator?
lines.cn: F：你是怎么知道这个驾驶模拟器的？

lines.t: M: My brother introduced it to me last year.
lines.cn: M：我哥哥去年介绍给我的。

lines.t: M: I was surprised to find how educational and realistic it was.
lines.cn: M：我惊讶地发现它既有教育意义又很逼真。

lines.t: M: It's called Euro Truck Simulator, but they have other versions as well for America and so on.
lines.cn: M：它叫《欧洲卡车模拟》，但他们还有其他版本，比如美国的等等。

lines.t: M: I was really drawn to the scenery.
lines.cn: M：我特别被里面的风景吸引。

lines.t: M: The routes go through parts of the country you don't normally see as a tourist.
lines.cn: M：这些路线会经过作为游客通常看不到的乡村地区。

lines.t: F: Yeah, I can see that.
lines.cn: F：是啊，我看得出来。

lines.t: F: It seems so simple, just transporting cargo from point A to point B, driving from one city to another.
lines.cn: F：它看起来很简单，就是把货物从 A 点运到 B 点，从一个城市开到另一个城市。

lines.t: F: But I really appreciate all the details that go into the game.
lines.cn: F：但我真的很欣赏游戏里那些用心的细节。

lines.t: F: It's even given me a new appreciation for the logistics industry and traffic on the road.
lines.cn: F：它甚至让我对物流行业和路上的交通有了新的敬意。

lines.t: M: I completely agree.
lines.cn: M：我完全同意。

lines.t: M: My brother also introduced me to some videos of someone that streams their game online.
lines.cn: M：我哥哥还给我看了些别人直播玩这个游戏的视频。

lines.t: M: It was fascinating to watch, really.
lines.cn: M：看着真有意思。

lines.t: M: This guy drove very carefully, obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules.
lines.cn: M：这家伙开得非常小心，遵守所有路标和交通规则。

lines.t: M: Such a contrast to most violent games.
lines.cn: M：和大多数暴力游戏形成鲜明对比。

lines.t: F: Honestly, playing has inspired me to look into the industry more.
lines.cn: F：说实话，玩这个让我想更多了解这个行业。

lines.t: F: I've read articles about how self-driving trucks may soon be available and could greatly impact cargo logistics.
lines.cn: F：我读到一些文章说自动驾驶卡车可能很快就会面世，并可能极大影响货物物流。

lines.t: F: Considering all that goes into driving these larger vehicles, it's amazing that we could soon have that kind of technology.
lines.cn: F：考虑到驾驶这些大型车辆涉及的一切，我们很快就能拥有那种技术，真了不起。

lines.t: M: Huh, I've gone one step further.
lines.cn: M：哈，我又往前走了一步。

lines.t: M: I registered to take a safe driving course to improve my real-life driving skills.
lines.cn: M：我报名参加了一个安全驾驶课程，以提高现实中开车的技术。

lines.t: M: In a way, I feel like I have a head start compared to other students in the class.
lines.cn: M：某种程度上，我觉得自己比班里其他学员有了先发优势。

lines.t: M: Playing this video game has given me some maneuvering practice already.
lines.cn: M：玩这个电子游戏已经让我练过一些操控了。

lines.t: F: I'm not sure how accurate the video game is compared to real-life situations, but if it results in more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection, I'd say that's a positive outcome.
lines.cn: F：我不确定这个游戏和现实情况相比有多准确，但如果它能让更多司机在进入路口前向两边看，那我会说这是个积极的结果。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the man say about his life of being self-employed?

options.A: It isn't so enjoyable as he expected.
options.B: It isn't so motivating as he believed.
options.C: It doesn't enable him to earn as much money as he used to.
options.D: It doesn't seem to offer as much freedom as he anticipated.

questions.cn: 关于他自由职业的生活，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它不像他期望的那么愉快。
optionsCn.B: 它不像他以为的那么有动力。
optionsCn.C: 它不能让他像以前那样挣那么多钱。
optionsCn.D: 它似乎没有提供他所预想的那么多自由。

questions.stem: What does the man say about managers?

options.A: Not all of them care about their employees' behaviors.
options.B: Few of them are aware of their employees' feelings.
options.C: Few of them offer praise and reward to their employees.
options.D: Not all of them know how to motivate their employees.

questions.cn: 关于经理们，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 并非所有经理都在意员工的行为。
optionsCn.B: 很少有经理察觉到员工的感受。
optionsCn.C: 很少有经理表扬和奖励员工。
optionsCn.D: 并非所有经理都知道如何激励员工。

questions.stem: What do both speakers value most about self-employment?

options.A: Job satisfaction.
options.B: Self-awareness.
options.C: Autonomy.
options.D: Money.

questions.cn: 两位说话人对自由职业最看重什么？

optionsCn.A: 工作满足感。
optionsCn.B: 自我意识。
optionsCn.C: 自主性。
optionsCn.D: 金钱。

questions.stem: On what point does the man agree with the woman? In this section, you'll hear two passages.

options.A: The importance of cultivating close relationships with clients.
options.B: The need for getting recommendations from their managers.
options.C: The advantages of permanent full-time employment.
options.D: The way to explore employees' interests and talents.

questions.cn: 在哪一点上男士同意女士的看法？

optionsCn.A: 与客户培养紧密关系的重要性。
optionsCn.B: 从经理那里获得推荐的必要性。
optionsCn.C: 固定全职工作的好处。
optionsCn.D: 发掘员工兴趣和才能的方式。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: How do you like being self-employed?
lines.cn: F：你觉得自由职业怎么样？

lines.t: M: There are obvious benefits, though I don't seem to have the freedom I anticipated, as I just don't seem able to decline work offers.
lines.cn: M：有明显的好处，不过我似乎并没有得到预想中的自由，因为我好像就是没法拒绝工作邀约。

lines.t: M: And working alone, there have been times when I've found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
lines.cn: M：而且独自工作时，我有时发现光靠钱提供的动力并不够。

lines.t: M: Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
lines.cn: M：你为自己工作以来有同样的感受吗？

lines.t: F: Sometimes, yes.
lines.cn: F：有时候有。

lines.t: F: Unlike the rest of the workforce, who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they're feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
lines.cn: F：和其他劳动者不同——他们有经理在感到懒散或无聊时激发动力——我们这些自由职业者工作时没有经理来提振情绪。

lines.t: F: There's no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
lines.cn: F：身边没人夸你，没人发起协作，没人更充分地发挥我们的兴趣和才能。

lines.t: M: That's a fact.
lines.cn: M：确实如此。

lines.t: M: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course.
lines.cn: M：当然，不是每个经理都有这样的意识和关照。

lines.t: M: And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
lines.cn: M：而且肯定不是所有经理都懂得如何激励人。

lines.t: M: Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there's an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
lines.cn: M：不过，身边有个经理至少说明：当你的精力和专注开始耗尽时，有机会指望他们足够好些来关照你。

lines.t: F: The motivator I value most is autonomy.
lines.cn: F：我最看重的激励因素是自主。

lines.t: F: I've learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
lines.cn: F：我学会了不因整天工作、对每个客户请求都说“好”而牺牲我珍视的自主。

lines.t: M: Yes, I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independents.
lines.cn: M：是的，我需要提醒自己：我选择这种生活方式是为了独立。

lines.t: M: I don't miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours, and so on.
lines.cn: M：我不怀念全职固定工作里我讨厌的那些方面，比如办公室政治、工作没保障、时间不灵活等等。

lines.t: M: I wouldn't mind a bit more in the form of praise, though.
lines.cn: M：不过，我倒是希望多一点表扬。

lines.t: M: Praise which is on the record.
lines.cn: M：有记录的表扬。

lines.t: F: That'll come with time.
lines.cn: F：那会随时间到来的。

lines.t: F: Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction, engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards.
lines.cn: F：关联感必然要通过人际互动来培养：与客户打交道、拿到书面评价和推荐、事后与客户保持联系。

lines.t: F: These are things you'll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation.
lines.cn: F：你会发现这些都会适时到来，并给你提供动力。

lines.t: M: You're right.
lines.cn: M：你说得对。

lines.t: M: That's an area I do need to put some more effort into, building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills.
lines.cn: M：这方面我确实需要多下些功夫——与那些使用我的服务和技能的人建立更紧密的关系。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the findings of the new study?

options.A: Consumers visualize their activities in different weather.
options.B: Good weather triggers consumers' desire to go shopping.
options.C: Weather conditions influence consumers' buying behavior.
options.D: Consumers' mental states change with the prices of goods.

questions.cn: 关于这项新研究的发现，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 消费者会在不同天气下想象自己的活动。
optionsCn.B: 好天气会引发消费者的购物欲。
optionsCn.C: 天气状况影响消费者的购买行为。
optionsCn.D: 消费者的心理状态随商品价格变化。

questions.stem: What does the passage say may increase the value of products for consumers?

options.A: Active consumption.
options.B: Direct correlation.
options.C: Individual association.
options.D: Mental visualization.

questions.cn: 文章说什么可能提升产品在消费者心中的价值？

optionsCn.A: 积极消费。
optionsCn.B: 直接关联。
optionsCn.C: 个体联想。
optionsCn.D: 心理想象。

questions.stem: How can the findings of the new study benefit online sellers according to the researchers?

options.A: Enabling them to simplify their mathematical formulas.
options.B: Helping them determine what to sell and at what price.
options.C: Enabling them to sell their products at a higher price.
options.D: Helping them advertise a greater variety of products.

questions.cn: 根据研究者，这项新研究的发现如何有益于线上卖家？

optionsCn.A: 使他们能简化自己的数学公式。
optionsCn.B: 帮他们确定卖什么、以什么价格卖。
optionsCn.C: 使他们能以更高价格出售产品。
optionsCn.D: 帮他们为更多种类的产品做广告。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there's little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
lines.cn: 天气是我们生活中一种持续的力量，但关于它如何影响商业的营销研究却很少。

lines.t: Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
lines.cn: 如今，一项新研究揭示了晴天和雪天如何影响消费者行为。

lines.t: Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
lines.cn: 这些天气条件会促使消费者在头脑中想象使用与相应天气相关的产品。

lines.t: This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
lines.cn: 这导致消费者对这些产品赋予更高的价值。

lines.t: That is, they're willing to pay more money for them.
lines.cn: 也就是说，他们愿意为它们花更多的钱。

lines.t: But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside.
lines.cn: 但这种相关性只在与户外活动相关的产品上被发现。

lines.t: How does this work?
lines.cn: 这是怎么发生的？

lines.t: Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
lines.cn: 研究者举了沙滩巾的例子。

lines.t: On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself.
lines.cn: 在晴天，看到该产品的消费者不只是在看这条沙滩巾本身。

lines.t: They are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
lines.cn: 他们很可能在想象自己躺在沙滩巾上晒太阳。

lines.t: This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumer's mind.
lines.cn: 这种使用沙滩巾的心理画面提升了该产品在消费者心中的价值。

lines.t: Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
lines.cn: 研究者提出以下假说来解释他们的发现。

lines.t: They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
lines.cn: 他们认为这种心理画面在晴天和雪天会起作用，因为这些天气条件与户外活动有正向关联。

lines.t: The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
lines.cn: 在下雨天则看不到这种效果。

lines.t: Researchers assert this is because there aren't many activities that are enabled by rain.
lines.cn: 研究者断言，这是因为雨天能促成的活动并不多。

lines.t: Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather and not for any activities.
lines.cn: 像雨伞这样与雨相关的大多数产品，只用于防雨，而非用于任何活动。

lines.t: Researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
lines.cn: 研究者认为，在网上销售各式各样产品的公司最能从这项研究提供的洞见中获益。

lines.t: Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price those products.
lines.cn: 线上卖家常用复杂的数学公式来决定推荐哪些产品、如何定价。

lines.t: Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
lines.cn: 纳入更多天气数据将使它们能做出更好的决策。

lines.t: This could bolster sales.
lines.cn: 这可能提升销量。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the accepted wisdom concerning the office environment?

options.A: A naturally ventilated office is more comfortable.
options.B: A cool office will boost employees' productivity.
options.C: Office air-conditioning should follow guidebooks.
options.D: Air-conditioning improves ventilation in the office.

questions.cn: 关于办公环境，公认的看法是什么？

optionsCn.A: 自然通风的办公室更舒适。
optionsCn.B: 凉爽的办公室会提升员工生产力。
optionsCn.C: 办公室空调应遵循指南。
optionsCn.D: 空调改善办公室的通风。

questions.stem: What did researchers find from their review of all studies relating to air conditioning and productivity?

options.A: People in their comfort zone of temperature are more satisfied with their productivity.
options.B: People in different countries vary in their tolerance to uncomfortable temperatures.
options.C: Twenty-two degrees is the optimal temperature for office workers.
options.D: There is a range of temperatures for people to feel comfortable.

questions.cn: 研究者对所有空调与生产力研究的综述发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 处在温度舒适区的人对自己的生产力更满意。
optionsCn.B: 不同国家的人对不适温度的耐受度不同。
optionsCn.C: 22 度是办公室职员的最优温度。
optionsCn.D: 存在一个让人感到舒适的温度区间。

questions.stem: What do we learn about using a little less air conditioning during hot weather?

options.A: It will have no negative impact on work.
options.B: It will be immediately noticeable.
options.C: It will sharply decrease work efficiency.
options.D: It will cause a lot of discomfort.

questions.cn: 关于在炎热天气少开一点空调，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它不会对工作产生负面影响。
optionsCn.B: 它会立刻被察觉。
optionsCn.C: 它会大幅降低工作效率。
optionsCn.D: 它会造成很多不适。

questions.stem: What happens when people are used to an air-conditioned environment?

options.A: They tend to favor lower temperatures.
options.B: They suffer from rapid temperature changes.
options.C: They are not bothered by temperature extremes.
options.D: They become less sensitive to high temperatures.

questions.cn: 当人们习惯空调环境后会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 他们倾向于偏好更低的温度。
optionsCn.B: 他们受温度骤变的困扰。
optionsCn.C: 他们不为极端温度所扰。
optionsCn.D: 他们对高温变得不那么敏感。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Setting the office air conditioning at about 22 degrees Celsius has become standard practice across the world.
lines.cn: 把办公室空调设在约 22 摄氏度，已成为世界各地的标准做法。

lines.t: Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation, and air conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
lines.cn: 世界各地许多关于供暖、通风与空调的指南都声称，办公室在 22 度时表现最佳。

lines.t: Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air-conditioned offices, but recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
lines.cn: 许多人确实在有空调的办公室里摆脱了夏季飙升的高温，但近期研究对“凉爽的办公室效率更高”这一公认看法提出了挑战。

lines.t: The reality is more complex.
lines.cn: 现实更为复杂。

lines.t: Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air conditioning and productivity.
lines.cn: 研究者对所有关于空调与生产力的研究做了综述。

lines.t: They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
lines.cn: 他们发现 22 度可能有点偏冷，即使在盛夏也是如此。

lines.t: For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees, and people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
lines.cn: 对穿着典型夏装的人来说，最佳温度范围应该在 23 到 26 度之间；只要能调整衣着和预期，人们甚至可以忍受超出这个舒适区的温度。

lines.t: In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air conditioning up.
lines.cn: 事实上，即使在很热的日子里，把空调调高一点也是合理的。

lines.t: People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot, but there is a range of at least 3 to 4 degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
lines.cn: 人们常常只追求某一个最优温度，在感到热的时候这可以理解，但至少有 3 到 4 度的区间不会带来任何不利影响。

lines.t: Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
lines.cn: 与此相关的另一个问题是，人们可能在心理上依赖空调。

lines.t: If they are used to the environment which is air-conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures, but the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
lines.cn: 如果他们习惯了有空调的环境，往往会偏好更低的温度，但研究发现，几乎所有人都能适应新温度。

lines.t: It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people's productivity suffered.
lines.cn: 只有在温度区间的极端两端，人们的生产力才会受损。

lines.t: This range was above 26 degrees and below 19 degrees.
lines.cn: 这个区间是高于 26 度和低于 19 度。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is one of the criticisms directed at the early research on solitude?

options.A: It overlooked the possibility that emotions may be controlled.
options.B: It ignored the fact that emotions are personal and subjective.
options.C: It classified emotions simply as either positive or negative.
options.D: It measured positive and negative emotions independently.

questions.cn: 针对早期独处研究的批评之一是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它忽略了情绪可能被控制的可能。
optionsCn.B: 它忽视了情绪是个人和主观的这一事实。
optionsCn.C: 它把情绪简单地分为积极或消极。
optionsCn.D: 它独立测量了积极和消极情绪。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the results of the new research?

options.A: Sitting alone without doing anything seemed really distressing.
options.B: Solitude adversely affected the participants' mental well-being.
options.C: Sitting alone for 15 minutes made the participants restless.
options.D: Solitude had a reductive effect on high-arousal emotions.

questions.cn: 关于这项新研究的结果，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 独自坐着什么都不做似乎很令人痛苦。
optionsCn.B: 独处对参与者的心理健康产生了不利影响。
optionsCn.C: 独自坐 15 分钟让参与者变得坐立不安。
optionsCn.D: 独处对高唤醒情绪有降低作用。

questions.stem: What did the second experiment in the new research find about solitude?

options.A: It proved hard to depict objectively.
options.B: It went hand in hand with sadness.
options.C: It helped increase low-arousal emotions.
options.D: It tended to intensify negative emotions.

questions.cn: 新研究中的第二项实验关于独处发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它被证明难以客观描述。
optionsCn.B: 它与悲伤如影随形。
optionsCn.C: 它有助于增强低唤醒情绪。
optionsCn.D: 它倾向于强化消极情绪。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience.
lines.cn: 心理学研究往往把独处描绘成一种负面体验。

lines.t: Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
lines.cn: 20 世纪 70 和 90 年代进行的研究显示，与别人在一起相比，人们独处时感觉更不快乐。

lines.t: However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
lines.cn: 然而，一篇新论文提出了关于独处的另一种观点：独处可以是积极的。

lines.t: Let's start by looking at the earlier research.
lines.cn: 我们先来看看早先的研究。

lines.t: It had a couple of shortcomings.
lines.cn: 它有几个缺陷。

lines.t: First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
lines.cn: 第一，它把情绪放在从积极到消极的单一刻度上测量，忽略了我们的积极情绪和消极情绪可能各自独立波动这一可能。

lines.t: Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
lines.cn: 另外，它把情绪简单地分为积极或消极。

lines.t: It didn't consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
lines.cn: 它没有考虑到：情绪唤起我们的程度不同，而积极和消极情绪都可能强烈或轻微地唤起我们。

lines.t: That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high arousal or low arousal.
lines.cn: 也就是说，无论积极还是消极，情绪都可能是高唤醒的或低唤醒的。

lines.t: High arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
lines.cn: 高唤醒情绪包括积极一端的兴奋或消极一端的愤怒，低唤醒情绪则包括积极一端的平静或消极一端的孤独。

lines.t: This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
lines.cn: 这项新研究试图克服这些缺陷。

lines.t: Researchers began with a simple study.
lines.cn: 研究者先做了一项简单的实验。

lines.t: They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity and measured how this solitude influenced their emotional state.
lines.cn: 他们请参与者在没有任何活动的情况下独自坐 15 分钟，并测量这种独处如何影响他们的情绪状态。

lines.t: This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high arousal emotions.
lines.cn: 这个实验特别想确定独处对高唤醒情绪的影响。

lines.t: It looked at positive emotions, such as being excited or interested, and negative emotions, including being scared or distressed.
lines.cn: 它考察了积极情绪，如兴奋或感兴趣，以及消极情绪，包括害怕或痛苦。

lines.t: The results were clear.
lines.cn: 结果很明确。

lines.t: After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
lines.cn: 独处 15 分钟后，参与者这两类情绪都下降了。

lines.t: A second study measured the effects of solitude on low arousal emotions.
lines.cn: 第二项研究测量了独处对低唤醒情绪的影响。

lines.t: These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad, or lonely.
lines.cn: 这些情绪既有积极的也有消极的，比如感到平静、放松、悲伤或孤独。

lines.t: That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
lines.cn: 该实验发现，所有这些情绪都因独处时间而增强。

lines.t: Thus, it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
lines.cn: 因此，过去对独处的描述似乎是错的。

lines.t: It doesn't have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
lines.cn: 独处并没有一种可以简单判定为好或坏的情绪效果。

lines.t: Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience.
lines.cn: 更确切地说，它改变我们内在体验的强度。

lines.t: It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
lines.cn: 它放大较安静的情绪，却削弱较强烈感受的强度。

lines.t: It's worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
lines.cn: 值得说明的是，这些发现针对的是相对短暂的独处。

lines.t: This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
lines.cn: 这与长期孤独截然不同。

lines.t: Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects.
lines.cn: 研究表明，后者与各种负面的身体和心理影响相关。

lines.t: How can people benefit from being alone?
lines.cn: 人们如何从独处中获益？

lines.t: The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
lines.cn: 这里的发现表明，人们可以利用独处来调节情绪。

lines.t: Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
lines.cn: 独处能帮我们在兴奋之后安静下来、在发怒之后平静下来，或者仅仅是感到安宁。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the brain when the body is at rest?

options.A: It uses up much less energy than it does in deep thinking.
options.B: It remains inactive without burning calories noticeably.
options.C: It continues to burn up calories to help us stay in shape.
options.D: It consumes almost a quarter of the body's total energy.

questions.cn: 关于身体静息时的大脑，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它消耗的能量比深度思考时少得多。
optionsCn.B: 它保持不活跃，不消耗可察觉的卡路里。
optionsCn.C: 它继续燃烧卡路里帮我们保持身材。
optionsCn.D: 它消耗全身总能量的近四分之一。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the consumption of the brain's energy?

options.A: Much of the consumption has nothing to do with conscious activities.
options.B: It has something to do with the difficulty of the activities in question.
options.C: Energy usage devoted to active learning accounts for a big part of it.
options.D: A significant amount of it is for performing difficult cognitive tasks.

questions.cn: 关于大脑的能量消耗，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 其中大部分消耗与有意识的活动无关。
optionsCn.B: 它与相关活动的难度有关。
optionsCn.C: 用于主动学习的能量占其中很大一部分。
optionsCn.D: 其中相当一部分用于执行困难的认知任务。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the overall energy availability in the brain?

options.A: It is believed to remain basically constant.
options.B: It is a prerequisite for any mental activity.
options.C: It is conducive to relieving mental exhaustion.
options.D: It is thought to be related to food consumption.

questions.cn: 关于大脑整体的能量供给，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它被认为基本保持恒定。
optionsCn.B: 它是任何脑力活动的先决条件。
optionsCn.C: 它有助于缓解脑力疲劳。
optionsCn.D: 它被认为与进食有关。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: In 1984, the World Chess Championships was called off abruptly due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
lines.cn: 1984 年，世界国际象棋锦标赛突然中断，原因是一位争夺冠军的棋手身体消瘦虚弱。

lines.t: He wasn't alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
lines.cn: 经历这项运动极端身体影响的并不只有他。

lines.t: Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6,000 calories in one day.
lines.cn: 据报道，顶尖棋手一天可以燃烧高达 6000 卡路里，这个数字简直离谱。

lines.t: Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
lines.cn: 这是否意味着，更费脑子地思考就是一条简单的减肥途径？

lines.t: Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20-25% of the overall energy.
lines.cn: 嗯，当身体处于静息状态时，我们知道大脑会消耗高达全身能量 20% 到 25%，这个比例惊人。

lines.t: This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body's weight overall.
lines.cn: 这样的消耗水平实际上让大脑成为身体里最耗能的器官，而它只占全身重量的 2%。

lines.t: So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we'll burn?
lines.cn: 那么，我们让这个器官工作得越多，燃烧的卡路里就越多？

lines.t: Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
lines.cn: 严格来说，对认知上有难度的任务，答案是肯定的。

lines.t: What counts as a difficult mental task varies between individuals, but generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
lines.cn: 什么算作困难的脑力任务因人而异，但大体上可以描述为：大脑无法用已学会的套路轻易解决的问题，或是条件不断变化的任务。

lines.t: However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack, because in relation to the brain's huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
lines.cn: 然而，深度思考并不会烧掉吃一块甜点摄入的卡路里，因为相对于大脑用于众多任务的巨大总能耗，光是“更费脑子地思考”所需的能量其实微不足道。

lines.t: We're unconscious of most of what uses up the brain's energy.
lines.cn: 大脑能量消耗的大部分，我们都意识不到。

lines.t: A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
lines.cn: 这些活动中有许多与“学会唱歌或弹吉他”这类有意识的活动无关。

lines.t: The brain is able to allocate blood and thus energy to particular regions that are being active at that point, but the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant.
lines.cn: 大脑能够向当时活跃的特定区域分配血液、从而分配能量，但大脑整体的能量供给据认为是恒定的。

lines.t: So while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain's energy budget overall, these activities don't significantly alter it.
lines.cn: 所以，虽然在进行困难的认知任务时，大脑局部区域的能量使用可能显著增加，但就整个大脑的能量预算而言，这些活动并不会显著改变它。

lines.t: So why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition?
lines.cn: 那么，那位国际象棋冠军为什么会瘦到无法参赛？

lines.t: The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
lines.cn: 普遍共识是，这主要归结于压力和进食减少，而不是脑力消耗。

lines.t: Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
lines.cn: 让身体长时间保持随时待命的状态，是非常耗能的。

lines.t: If you can't eat as often or as much as you can or would normally, then you might lose weight.
lines.cn: 如果你不能像平常那样规律或足量进食，就可能掉体重。

tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the job interview question, tell me about yourself?

options.A: Job candidates rarely take it seriously.
options.B: Job seekers tend to have a ready answer.
options.C: Job seekers often feel at a loss where to start in answering it.
options.D: Job candidates can respond freely due to its open-ended nature.

questions.cn: 关于「请介绍一下你自己」这个面试问题，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 求职者很少认真对待它。
optionsCn.B: 求职者往往有现成的答案。
optionsCn.C: 求职者常常不知从何开始回答。
optionsCn.D: 由于它的开放性，求职者可以自由作答。

questions.stem: What will most people do when they come to a job interview?

options.A: Follow their career coaches' guidelines.
options.B: Strive to take control of their narrative.
options.C: Do their best to impress the interviewer.
options.D: Repeat the information on their resume.

questions.cn: 大多数人去面试时会怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 遵循职业教练的指导方针。
optionsCn.B: 努力掌控自己的叙事。
optionsCn.C: 尽力给面试官留下好印象。
optionsCn.D: 重复简历上的信息。

questions.stem: Why should job seekers talk with partners, friends, and co-workers?

options.A: To reflect on their past achievements as well as failures.
options.B: To produce examples for different interview questions.
options.C: To discuss important details they are going to present.
options.D: To identify a broad general strength to elaborate on.

questions.cn: 求职者为什么应该和伴侣、朋友、同事聊聊？

optionsCn.A: 为了反思自己过去的成就与失败。
optionsCn.B: 为不同面试问题准备事例。
optionsCn.C: 讨论自己将要呈现的重要细节。
optionsCn.D: 找出一个可以展开的宽泛优势。

questions.stem: What other important preparations should job seekers make before an interview? That's the end of listening comprehension.

options.A: Getting acquainted with the human resources personnel.
options.B: Finding out why the company provides the job opening.
options.C: Figuring out what benefits the company is able to offer them.
options.D: Tailoring their expectations to the company's long-term goal.

questions.cn: 面试前求职者还应该做哪些重要准备？

optionsCn.A: 结识人力资源人员。
optionsCn.B: 弄清公司为何提供这个岗位。
optionsCn.C: 弄清公司能给他们什么好处。
optionsCn.D: 把期望调整到贴合公司的长期目标。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Tell me about yourself.
lines.cn: 请介绍一下你自己。

lines.t: May seem like an easy job interview question, but the open-ended nature of this question often leaves job seekers at a loss where to start.
lines.cn: 这看似是个简单的求职面试问题，但这个问题的开放性常常让求职者不知从何说起。

lines.t: This common question is actually a critical test of a job candidate's communication skills, so it's important not to give an unprepared response or mess it up.
lines.cn: 这个常见问题其实是求职者沟通能力的关键考验，所以重要的是不要给出未经准备的回答，也不要把它搞砸。

lines.t: Tell me about yourself is often the first question professional career coaches prepare people for when they give interview guidance.
lines.cn: 在做面试辅导时，「请介绍一下你自己」往往是职业教练让人准备的第一道题。

lines.t: It's the opportunity for the candidate to take control of the narrative and tell their story in a way that really matters to their audience.
lines.cn: 这是求职者掌控叙事、以真正对听众重要的方式讲述自己故事的机会。

lines.t: It takes hard work and extensive preparation to answer this question well.
lines.cn: 要答好这个问题，需要下功夫和大量准备。

lines.t: When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their resume, so they don't need to repeat the information.
lines.cn: 一个人去面试时，面试官想必已看过他的简历，所以他不需要重复简历上的信息。

lines.t: But that's what most people will do, as it's their instinct to recite things that are already on their resume.
lines.cn: 但这恰恰是大多数人会做的，因为复述简历上已有的内容是一种本能。

lines.t: It's important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
lines.cn: 求职者需要在两个关键方面做足功课。

lines.t: First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves.
lines.cn: 第一，他们不只是在告诉别人一个关于自己的事实。

lines.t: They're telling a story, and stories take work to create.
lines.cn: 他们在讲一个故事，而故事需要花功夫去构建。

lines.t: Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments something they're proud of and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
lines.cn: 讲出一个好故事，意味着要反思：是什么让自己的职业成就值得自豪，这些成就又凸显了哪些优势。

lines.t: Candidates shouldn't pick a broad general strength to elaborate on, such as, I'm smart, I work hard, and I get things done.
lines.cn: 求职者不应挑一个宽泛笼统的优势来展开，比如“我聪明、我勤奋、我能把事办成”。

lines.t: To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends, or co-workers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
lines.cn: 为了应对不同面试问题准备出多个职业成就或事例，求职者应当和他人聊聊，尤其是了解自己的人——伴侣、朋友或同事，他们会想起一些本人记不得的故事。

lines.t: Secondly, candidates should know what's at stake for the opening.
lines.cn: 第二，求职者应当明白这个空缺岗位的关键利益在哪里。

lines.t: What they really are asking you is, tell me why you are going to help me.
lines.cn: 面试官真正在问你的是：说说你为什么会帮到我。

lines.t: If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
lines.cn: 如果求职者做了准备，这些事他们早就该弄清楚了。

lines.t: They've read the job description and researched the company on the internet.
lines.cn: 他们读过了职位描述，也在网上调研过这家公司。

lines.t: What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish, and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
lines.cn: 求职者应当关注的是：这家公司在做什么、想达成什么，以及是什么在阻碍他们达成。

lines.t: How long should it take to answer?
lines.cn: 回答该用多长时间？

lines.t: Around a minute.
lines.cn: 大约一分钟。

lines.t: That's about right for most people's attention spans.
lines.cn: 对大多数人的注意力持续时间来说，这个长度比较合适。

lines.t: Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes will start to feel more like a speech.
lines.cn: 不到一分钟会显得仓促，超过两分钟则开始更像一篇演讲。

lines.t: But the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
lines.cn: 但回答的长度并不是精确的科学，求职者需要让自己的职业故事保持聚焦，并贴合听众。
